title: Harmonize lease signaling across SDKs and add iterable guardrails
author: Marta Nguyen
description: Context: We have recurring inconsistencies between Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs around session lease signals (heartbeat vs explicit lease refresh) and a class of bugs where consumers accidentally iterate streams twice or fail to observe token-rotation handshakes. Motivation: Reduce subtle production failures, make retry/lease defaults predictable, and bring ergonomic safety to streaming consumers without breaking existing syncs. Summary: This PR centralizes the lease/heartbeat handshake semantics into a small cross-SDK contract and implements local 'iterable guardrails' wrappers in each SDK to detect and fail-fast on common misuse patterns. It also unifies a compact retry profile name ("compact:fast-3") and makes it the recommended default for short-lived streaming interactions. Changes span Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, docs, and changelogs. Commits: - python: add LeaseSignalMiddleware, iterable_guard decorator, tests for double-iteration detection - typescript: implement IterableGuard class, lease-signal adapter, unit tests and docs snippets - go: introduce session/guard package, compact retry profile, examples and integration test - common: move retry profile helper into sdk-common, update config and README - docs: update streaming.md and quickstarts showing recommended patterns - chore: bump py-sdk v0.9.8, ts-sdk v1.7.3, go-sdk v1.5.0 and update changelogs Files changed (high level): sdks/python/src/session.py, sdks/python/src/streaming/iterable_guard.py, sdks/python/tests/test_lease_handshake.py, sdks/typescript/src/iterable_guard.ts, sdks/typescript/src/lease_adapter.ts, sdks/go/session/guard.go, sdk-common/retry/profiles.go, docs/sdk/streaming.md Reasoning: The middleware/adapter approach keeps the runtime lightweight while ensuring the same observable behavior across languages. Iterable guards are deliberately opt-out via a feature flag to preserve backwards compatibility for advanced consumers. CI and tests: Initial CI run failed lint in TypeScript (prettier) and a flaky Go test; both were addressed in follow-up commits. Final CI: all unit and integration tests passed on main matrix (linux/amd64, windows/amd64, macos/arm64). Migration notes: - No breaking API changes; opt-out available through SDK config: enableIterableGuard=false - If you relied on the previous implicit lease refresh behavior, switch to explicit LeaseSignalMiddleware or update to the new compact retry profile. Release notes: Adds cross-SDK lease handshake contract and optional iterable misuse guard; recommends compact retry profile for short streaming calls. Merge: squash and merge (maintains small commit history and clear changelog entry).

review_comments: Ethan Kline: Can we avoid adding a global runtime allocation in the Python iterable guard? Suggest using a weakref set instead of a strong registry.
Marta Nguyen: Switched to weakref-based registry in the second commit; added benchmarks showing negligible overhead.
Priya Shah: Were there any observed regressions in latency for short streaming calls after adding the lease handshake? If so, we should make the default opt-in.
Marta Nguyen: Measured median token latency is unchanged within noise; default is opt-out (enableIterableGuard=false) per discussion and docs updated.
